note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: Is this pump throttled by a control valve when it could run on a variable speed drive?

evidence.text: equipment P-900 reads "P-900 Water transfer pump"
valve FV-900 reads "FV-900 Discharge flow control valve" at P-900
no speed control (SC, SIC, SY tag, VFD or VSD) on or next to the pump
Pump rated flow and head: P-900 CAPACITY = 100 gpm
Pump rated flow and head: P-900 DISCHARGE = 90 ft
Motor rating and speed: P-900 HP = 10
Motor rating and speed: P-900 RPM = 1750
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: P-900 pump_curve_uri = P-901-curve.pdf
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: P-900 pump_curve_asset = P-901
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: P-900 pump_curve_readable = False
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: P-900 motor_efficiency = {'value': 0.9, 'basis': 'unreviewed nameplate transcription; motor identity unknown'}

data_requests.item: Control valve position (% open) over normal operation
where: historian or DCS trend for FV-900 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
DCS/PLC configuration: the valve's controller output
a walkdown: read the positioner stroke indicator at several rates
data_requests.how: Take a month or more of valve output at normal sampling; note the typical and the lowest % open, and the hours at each.

data_requests.item: Flow over the same period (a flow-duration curve)
where: site records: production rate records
data_requests.how: Bin the flow into ranges and count the hours in each.

where: a walkdown: elevations and pressures at the suction source and the delivery point
site records: line list or isometrics for pipe lengths and sizes
data_requests.how: Static head = lift plus pressure difference between source and destination; the rest of the pump head at duty is friction plus the valve drop.

data_requests.item: Matched pump curve, rated duty and system operating points
where: the vendor datasheet: pump curve and rated duty point
the pump nameplate on P-900
data_requests.how: Retain supplied ratings as unverified candidates. Review the curve against pump identity, installed impeller, speed, fluid, axes/units and revision; distinguish rated duty, BEP and actual operating points. A rating, URI or readability flag does not establish a matching curve or system suitability.

data_requests.item: Motor nameplate, efficiency and drive basis
where: the motor nameplate on P-900
maintenance records: motor record card
data_requests.how: Review existing nameplate or motor records for identity, rated shaft output in original units, speed, full-load efficiency and drive/bypass basis. HP/RPM alone do not establish efficiency or measured electrical input; retain missing or ambiguous evidence.

value.basis: unreviewed nameplate transcription; motor identity unknown

questions.decision_rule: Worth a drive quote when the valve normally runs well throttled for long hours and most of the head is friction rather than static lift (VSDs suit friction-dominated systems best). Close it if the valve normally runs near fully open, the head is mostly static, or the pump runs few hours.

typical_benefit.wording: "With rotodynamic pump installations, savings of between 30% and 50% have been achieved in many installations by installing VSDs." Also: "It is estimated that 75% of pump systems are oversized, many by more than 20%."
typical_benefit.arc: 2.4146 (IAC/ITAC browse page: 5,227 recommendations, 3.0 yr average payback, 31.4% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)
source_titles: S15: Variable Speed Pumping: A Guide to Successful Applications, Executive Summary (DOE ITP with Europump/HI, DOE/GO-102004-1913, May 2004)
S24: DOE IAC/ITAC database: browse pages, download, schema document

questions.limits: On a hand-built model the valve sits on a stream leaving the pump. On an extracted drawing the links have no direction, so the rule takes a control valve within four drawn links that do not pass through other equipment; it may still be on a branch or the suction side, so check the drawing. IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers.

questions.question: Is this pump oversized, given a bypass line around it or its valve?

evidence.text: equipment P-900 reads "P-900 Water transfer pump"
hand valve HV-900 reads "HV-900 Pump bypass valve" at P-900
Pump stated rated flow and head: P-900 CAPACITY = 100 gpm
Pump stated rated flow and head: P-900 DISCHARGE = 90 ft
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: P-900 pump_curve_uri = P-901-curve.pdf
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: P-900 pump_curve_asset = P-901
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: P-900 pump_curve_readable = False

data_requests.item: Measured flow and head at normal operation
where: a walkdown: suction and discharge pressure gauges plus a clamp-on ultrasonic flow meter
data_requests.how: Read flow and suction and discharge pressure at steady operation.

data_requests.item: How often the bypass is open
where: a walkdown: valve position and line temperature
site records: operator logs
data_requests.how: Record bypass position over several shifts.

data_requests.item: Matched pump curve and best-efficiency-point (BEP) duty
where: the vendor datasheet: pump curve
data_requests.how: Review the matching curve for installed impeller, speed, fluid and units, then identify its BEP flow/head with source revision and locator. Keep generic CAPACITY/DISCHARGE as rated candidates, not BEP. Retain unknown or unsuitable curve evidence and compare with representative measured operation.

questions.decision_rule: Prioritize the pump if it runs at a flow 30% or more away from BEP or the bypass is used routinely; otherwise close it.

typical_benefit.wording: Five indications: "excessive flow noise, highly throttled flow control valves, heavy use of bypass lines, frequent replacements of bearings and seals, and intermittent pump operation." Prioritize pumps "with flow rates of 30% or more from the BEP flow rates, or with system imbalances greater than 20%." No % saving stated.
source_titles: S13: Improving Pumping System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry, 2nd ed. (DOE + Hydraulic Institute; DOE/GO-102006-2079)
S14: Pumping Systems Tip #6, Match Pumps to System Requirements (DOE/GO-102005-2160)

questions.limits: A drawn bypass may be normally closed; the drawing cannot show how it is used.

questions.question: Is this motor oversized for its load?

evidence.text: equipment P-900 reads "P-900 Water transfer pump"
Motor rated power: P-900 HP = 10
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: P-900 RPM = 1750
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: P-900 motor_efficiency = {'value': 0.9, 'basis': 'unreviewed nameplate transcription; motor identity unknown'}

data_requests.item: Measured input power or current at normal load
where: site records: approved existing motor input-power and representative load/production records
data_requests.how: Retain representative period, coverage, load timing and measurement basis. Prefer documented input kW; three-phase watts derived from voltage/current also need power factor and phase basis. Current alone is unreliable at low load. No new live measurements are instructed; record unavailable evidence.

data_requests.item: Motor nameplate, rated output and full-load efficiency
where: the motor nameplate on P-900
maintenance records: motor record card
data_requests.how: Review identity, rated shaft output in original units, full-load efficiency, rated speed/current and source revision. HP alone cannot settle the efficiency needed by the load calculation. Stated output is not measured electrical input; retain unknown efficiency rather than supplying a default.

value.basis: unreviewed nameplate transcription; motor identity unknown

questions.decision_rule: Load factor = measured input power divided by (rated output divided by rated efficiency). A motor running well below about 40% of full load is worth a resize question; one oversized slightly is fine.

typical_benefit.wording: "At loads below 40% of full load, motor efficiency begins to decline dramatically." "Slightly oversizing a motor (up to 25%) can actually increase efficiency." No % saving stated.
typical_benefit.arc: 2.41xx (category only) (IAC/ITAC browse page: motors: 18,002 recommendations, 2.5 yr average payback, 52.3% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)
source_titles: S16: Improving Motor and Drive System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry (DOE/GO-102014-4356, Feb 2014; prepared by WSU Energy Program + NREL)
S24: DOE IAC/ITAC database: browse pages, download, schema document

questions.limits: Fires only where the drawing carries a motor rating field (filled or blank); a drawing without one gives no trigger. IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers.

questions.question: Is heat rejected to cooling water at a temperature another user could use?

evidence.text: equipment E-900 reads "E-900 Process cooler with cooling water"
Cooling water supply temperature: E-900 cooling_water_C = 20
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: E-900 CAPACITY = 100 gpm

where: a walkdown: thermometer on the return
data_requests.how: Record at normal operation; the return temperature is the grade of the heat on offer.

data_requests.item: Temperature of the stream being cooled (in and out)
where: site records: heat and material balance
the vendor datasheet: exchanger datasheet
site records: heat and material balance
data_requests.how: Review exchanger identity, units and rated-versus-actual basis. A generic CAPACITY may denote flow or design capacity, not heat duty. Retain coincident flow, heat-capacity basis and inlet/return temperatures over a stated period, or a documented heat balance; supplied scalars do not establish usable recovered heat.

data_requests.item: A heat user that needs heat below the return temperature
where: site records: list of heating duties with temperatures
a walkdown: users nearby
data_requests.how: Match by temperature, hours and distance.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a study only if the heat leaves hotter than a nearby user needs, for overlapping hours; cooling water returning only a few degrees above ambient closes it.

typical_benefit.wording: Closest source wording (S19, pinch): potential "far exceeds that from well-known conventional techniques such as heat recovery from boiler flue gas, insulation and steam trap management." No % stated. For air compressors S11 says recovery "anywhere from 50 to 90 percent" of the heat, which applies to compressors only.
source_titles: S19: Worrell & Galitsky, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for Petroleum Refineries: An ENERGY STAR Guide (LBNL-56183, Feb 2005)
S11: Improving Compressed Air System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry, 3rd ed. (DOE + Compressed Air Challenge)

questions.limits: Does not fire on equipment that cools the cooling water itself (a cooling water cooler, air-cooled exchanger or cooling tower): that equipment rejects the loop's heat, it does not receive process heat.
